PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Wudhu is the washing that lifts minor ritual impurity so that a Muslim may pray. In this sub-strand you will learn what breaks wudhu, when a Muslim should be in wudhu, and why staying pure matters for ibadah.

## Strand 4.0: Devotional Acts
Sub-strand 4.1.2: Wudhu (Ablution)
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) state the nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) to maintain a state of ritual purity
b) assess the significance of wudhu in the life of a Muslim
c) value the need to be in a state of purity as a condition for ibadah

## Key inquiry questions
1. What nullifies wudhu?
2. Why is it important to be in a state of wudhu?
3. When is it recommended to be in a state of wudhu?

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skill of writing is enhanced as learners search for nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook.
• Self-efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners discuss times recommended to be in a state of wudhu and present in class.

## Values
• Unity: cooperation enhanced as learners discuss the importance of maintaining wudhu, in pairs or groups.
• Responsibility: hard work enhanced as learners search for nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) using digital devices/from resource books and write in their notebook.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Personal hygiene as learners perform wudhu.

## Links to other learning areas
• Agriculture as learners observe and maintain ritual purity.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 4.0 Devotional Acts, Sub-strand 4.1.2 Wudhu (Ablution)
• Sahih Muslim: sins leaving with wudhu, and the ghurra of the Prophet’s community
• Sunan Abu Dawud: the advice to make wudhu when angry

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: What nullifies wudhu

LESSON 1: WHAT NULLIFIES WUDHU
==============================

## What you will learn
• State the nullifiers of wudhu.
• Distinguish a deep sleep from a light nap.
• Explain what a person does after wudhu is broken.

Curriculum outcomes: a) state the nullifiers of wudhu (ablution) to maintain a state of ritual purity

## Introduction
You finished wudhu for Dhuhr, then fell deeply asleep until Asr. Are you still in wudhu? A nullifier is something that breaks wudhu and means it must be performed again before swalah.

## Notes
### Minor impurity
Wudhu removes hadath asghar, the minor ritual impurity. It does not replace a full bath, ghusl, when ghusl is required. While wudhu remains, a person may pray. When a nullifier happens, the wudhu ends, even if the face still looks wet.

### Nullifiers to write in your notebook
1. Anything that comes out of the two private passages, such as urine, stool or wind.
2. Deep sleep, in which a person no longer knows what is happening around them.
3. Fainting, or anything else that takes away the mind in a similar way.
4. Touching the private parts with the palm of the bare hand, without a covering.

A light nap while you are sitting and can still hear the people around you does not, by itself, break wudhu. Deep sleep does. Eating ordinary food, such as bread or fruit, does not break wudhu. Bleeding from a small scratch is najasa to wash off the skin, but in the teaching followed here it is not listed as a nullifier of wudhu. Do not add extra nullifiers from guesswork.

### After a nullifier
If you want to pray, perform wudhu again with water. If you are already in swalah and you are certain that wudhu has broken, you stop and make wudhu, then pray again. A mere doubt, with no certainty, does not cancel a wudhu you know you had. Shaytan uses endless doubt to disturb people. Be honest about what you are sure of, then either renew wudhu or continue with confidence.

Search these nullifiers in your IRE book or in a lesson the teacher shows you, and write them in your own words so that you can state them without the page.

## Key words
• wudhu — ablution; the washing that removes minor ritual impurity
• nullifier — something that breaks wudhu
• hadath asghar — minor ritual impurity, removed by wudhu

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Four things happen to four learners: one passes wind, one dozes while still hearing the lesson, one faints, and one eats a banana. Whose wudhu has broken?

Working:
1. Wind from the private passage nullifies wudhu.
2. A light nap in which the person still hears does not.
3. Fainting nullifies wudhu. Eating a banana does not.

Answer: The wudhu of the learner who passed wind and the learner who fainted has broken. The light nap and the banana have not broken it.

## Activity: Search and write the nullifiers
You will need: IRE textbook or a digital passage chosen by the teacher, Notebook
1. Search the nullifiers of wudhu from the textbook or from the digital material your teacher opens.
2. Write the nullifiers in your notebook in a numbered list.
3. In pairs, test each other with examples: deep sleep, light nap, urine, ordinary food.
4. Correct the list so that it matches the four nullifiers of this lesson.

## Practice
1. List four nullifiers of wudhu.
2. Does a light nap, while you can still hear people, break wudhu?
3. What must a person do before swalah if wudhu has broken and water is available?

## Summary
• Wudhu breaks when something exits the private passages, when sleep is deep, when the mind is lost, or when the private parts are touched with the bare palm.
• A light nap and ordinary food do not break wudhu.
• After a nullifier, wudhu is performed again before swalah.

### Answers to practice
1. Urine, stool or wind; deep sleep; fainting or loss of the mind; touching the private parts with the bare palm.
2. No. Deep sleep, in which you no longer know what is happening, does break it.
3. Perform wudhu again.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Times when wudhu is needed or recommended

LESSON 2: TIMES WHEN WUDHU IS NEEDED OR RECOMMENDED
===================================================

## What you will learn
• Distinguish when wudhu is required from when it is recommended.
• Name the recommended times to be in a state of wudhu.
• Explain one benefit of each time.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of wudhu in the life of a Muslim

## Introduction
Wudhu is not only a door into swalah. The Prophet (S.A.W.) loved to be in a state of purity at other times as well. Some of those times are required. Others are strongly recommended.

## Notes
### When wudhu is required
Wudhu is required before swalah if you are in minor impurity. Without it, the prayer has not met its condition of purity. Wudhu is also required, in the teaching followed in this curriculum, before you touch the Arabic mushaf, the copy of the Qur’an. A translation book used in an English lesson is not the same as the mushaf, but the mushaf itself is touched in a state of purity.

### Times that are recommended
It is recommended to be in wudhu:

- Before you sleep. The Prophet (S.A.W.) liked to sleep in a state of wudhu.
- When you enter the mosque.
- When you sit to make dua or dhikr.
- When you renew wudhu after a nullifier even before the next adhan, so that you are ready.
- When you are angry. It is reported that the Prophet (S.A.W.) advised the angry person to make wudhu (Abu Dawud), because anger is stirred by Shaytan and cooling water helps the person to calm down.

### Why the times matter
Required wudhu protects the validity of swalah. Recommended wudhu keeps the tongue and the body ready for worship and trains a habit of cleanliness. A learner who sleeps in wudhu and wakes for Fajr has fewer delays. A learner who makes wudhu when angry is less likely to say a word that Raqib and Atid will record as a sin.

Present these times clearly: one list for “must” and one list for “should”. Mixing them up makes people think sleep without wudhu is a sin like praying without wudhu. It is not. It is a missed reward, while swalah without wudhu is not valid.

## Key words
• mushaf — a copy of the Qur’an in Arabic
• recommended — a sunnah practice that brings reward but is not the same as a condition of swalah

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Sort these into required or recommended: wudhu before Dhuhr, wudhu before sleep, wudhu before touching the mushaf, wudhu when angry.

Working:
1. Swalah and touching the mushaf require wudhu in this lesson.
2. Sleep and anger are recommended times.
3. Both kinds are good. Only the required ones decide validity.

Answer: Required: before Dhuhr and before touching the mushaf. Recommended: before sleep and when angry.

## Activity: Two lists to present
You will need: Manila paper, Notebook
1. In groups, draw two columns: Required and Recommended.
2. Place each time from the lesson in the correct column.
3. Present the chart to the class and answer one question from another group.
4. Write both lists in your notebook.

## Practice
1. Name two situations in which wudhu is required in this lesson.
2. Name three recommended times to be in wudhu.
3. Is sleeping without wudhu the same as praying without wudhu?

## Summary
• Wudhu is required for swalah and, in this teaching, for touching the mushaf.
• It is recommended before sleep, at the mosque, during dua, and when angry.
• Required and recommended times are both valuable, and they are not the same.

### Answers to practice
1. Before swalah if one is in minor impurity, and before touching the mushaf.
2. Any three: before sleep, when entering the mosque, when making dua or dhikr, after renewing it so as to stay ready, or when angry.
3. No. Sleeping in wudhu is recommended. Swalah without wudhu, when wudhu is required, is not valid.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Why wudhu matters

LESSON 3: WHY WUDHU MATTERS
===========================

## What you will learn
• Give the benefits of performing and keeping wudhu.
• Explain the Hadith about the shining marks of wudhu.
• Show that purity is valued as a condition for ibadah.

Curriculum outcomes: b) assess the significance of wudhu in the life of a Muslim; c) value the need to be in a state of purity as a condition for ibadah

## Introduction
On the Day of Judgement the Prophet (S.A.W.) will recognise his community by a light on the parts they used to wash. That Hadith shows why a learner should value wudhu even when nobody at the tap is watching.

## Notes
### Benefits you can explain
Wudhu matters for these reasons:

- It is the key to swalah. Minor impurity is lifted and the condition of purity is met.
- It cleans the face, mouth, nose, hands and feet, so it is also personal hygiene.
- The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that sins leave with the water of a correct wudhu, or with its last drop (Muslim). The washing is not a magic trick. It is obedience, and Allah forgives by His mercy.
- He also said that his community will come on the Day of Judgement with brightness on their faces, hands and feet from the traces of wudhu (Muslim). Those marks are called ghurra.
- Staying in wudhu keeps you ready for the next prayer and for dua.
- Renewing wudhu after a nullifier trains honesty. You do not stand in the row pretending.

### Valuing the state of purity
A person values wudhu by learning what breaks it, by performing it properly when water is there, and by not treating it as a bother. If water is truly unavailable, Islamic teaching has tayammum, which you will meet in later study. You do not invent a dry wipe of the face and call it wudhu. While water is available, use it.

Write the benefits in your notebook in your own sentences. The aim is to assess them, not only to memorise a list: each benefit should answer the question, “Why does a Muslim want to be in wudhu?”

## Key words
• ghurra — the brightness on the face and limbs of the Prophet’s community from wudhu
• tayammum — dry ablution with clean earth, used only when water cannot be used

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A girl says, “My face is already clean from the morning wash, so I do not need wudhu for Asr.” Assess her statement.

Working:
1. Ordinary cleanliness is not the same as wudhu.
2. If a nullifier has happened, wudhu must be renewed for swalah.
3. Even the reward and the marks of wudhu belong to the ritual washing done as worship.

Answer: A morning wash does not replace wudhu. If her wudhu has broken, she performs wudhu again before Asr.

## Activity: Write the importance of wudhu
You will need: Notebook
1. In pairs, discuss why it is important to maintain wudhu.
2. Agree on at least four points, including swalah, hygiene, forgiveness and the marks on the Day of Judgement.
3. Be guided by the teacher to correct any point that is not accurate.
4. Write the final points in your notebook.

## Practice
1. State two benefits of wudhu besides having a shiny face in the morning.
2. What is ghurra in the Hadith of wudhu?
3. Why should a Muslim value being in a state of purity?

## Summary
• Wudhu makes swalah possible, cleans the limbs, and is a cause of forgiveness.
• The Prophet’s community will shine from the traces of wudhu.
• Valuing purity means renewing wudhu honestly when it breaks.

### Answers to practice
1. It makes swalah valid when minor impurity had been present, and Allah forgives sins through a correct wudhu. It also leaves the marks of ghurra.
2. The brightness on the faces and limbs by which the Prophet’s community will be known, from the traces of wudhu.
3. Because purity is a condition for swalah and other ibadah, and because wudhu brings cleanliness, forgiveness and readiness to worship.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 4.1.2 WUDHU (ABLUTION)
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which of these nullifies wudhu?
   A. Eating a banana
   B. Passing wind
   C. A light nap while you still hear the class
   D. Smiling

2. Deep sleep breaks wudhu because…
   A. The sleeper always dreams
   B. The person no longer knows what is happening and control is lost
   C. Sleep is najasa mughalladha
   D. Pillows are impure

3. What is the ruling, in this lesson, on touching the private parts with the bare palm?
   A. Is a sunnah of wudhu
   B. Nullifies wudhu in the teaching of this lesson
   C. Replaces water
   D. Is required before sleep

4. Wudhu is required before…
   A. Swalah, if you are in minor impurity
   B. Every drink of water
   C. Opening a mathematics book
   D. Racing in the field

5. Which time is recommended rather than a condition of the prayer?
   A. Wudhu before Fajr if you need it
   B. Wudhu before going to sleep
   C. Removing najasa from the shirt
   D. Facing the Qibla

6. Where is the advice to make wudhu when angry reported?

7. Ghurra means…
   A. A type of najasa
   B. Brightness from the traces of wudhu on the Day of Judgement
   C. The call to prayer
   D. A nullifier

8. Why is a correct wudhu linked with forgiveness?
   A. Water itself is an angel
   B. The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that sins leave with the wudhu
   C. It replaces tawbah forever
   D. It cancels the need to pray

9. You are sure you had wudhu, then you only imagine that it might have broken. What do you do?
   A. You must repeat every prayer of the week
   B. Certainty of wudhu is not removed by a mere doubt
   C. You stop praying for the day
   D. You use soil while water is beside you

10. What does it mean to value purity as a condition for ibadah?
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 4.1.2 WUDHU (ABLUTION)
========================================

1. B. Passing wind
   What exits from the private passages, including wind, breaks wudhu.

2. B. The person no longer knows what is happening and control is lost
   Deep sleep is a nullifier. A light nap in which you still hear people is not.

3. B. Nullifies wudhu in the teaching of this lesson
   It is listed among the nullifiers to write in the notebook.

4. A. Swalah, if you are in minor impurity
   Purity is a condition of swalah. Touching the mushaf also requires wudhu in this teaching.

5. B. Wudhu before going to sleep
   Sleeping in wudhu is a recommended sunnah. Praying without required wudhu is not valid.

6. Sunan Abu Dawud.
   It is a recommended help for calming anger, not a fifth pillar of swalah.

7. B. Brightness from the traces of wudhu on the Day of Judgement
   The Prophet (S.A.W.) described his community as recognisable by these marks. The Hadith is in Sahih Muslim.

8. B. The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that sins leave with the wudhu
   Sahih Muslim reports the forgiveness connected with performing wudhu properly.

9. B. Certainty of wudhu is not removed by a mere doubt
   A real nullifier breaks wudhu. A passing doubt does not.

10. Performing wudhu properly before swalah and renewing it after a nullifier, because the prayer depends on that purity.
   Wudhu is not an optional extra when minor impurity is present.

2. If a nullifier has happened, wudhu must be renewed for swalah.
3. Even the reward and the marks of wudhu belong to the ritual washing done as worship.

Answer: A morning wash does not replace wudhu. If her wudhu has broken, she performs wudhu again before Asr.

## Activity: Write the importance of wudhu
You will need: Notebook
1. In pairs, discuss why it is important to maintain wudhu.
2. Agree on at least four points, including swalah, hygiene, forgiveness and the marks on the Day of Judgement.
3. Be guided by the teacher to correct any point that is not accurate.
4. Write the final points in your notebook.

## Practice
1. State two benefits of wudhu besides having a shiny face in the morning.
2. What is ghurra in the Hadith of wudhu?
3. Why should a Muslim value being in a state of purity?

## Summary
• Wudhu makes swalah possible, cleans the limbs, and is a cause of forgiveness.
• The Prophet’s community will shine from the traces of wudhu.
• Valuing purity means renewing wudhu honestly when it breaks.

### Answers to practice
1. It makes swalah valid when minor impurity had been present, and Allah forgives sins through a correct wudhu. It also leaves the marks of ghurra.
2. The brightness on the faces and limbs by which the Prophet’s community will be known, from the traces of wudhu.
3. Because purity is a condition for swalah and other ibadah, and because wudhu brings cleanliness, forgiveness and readiness to worship.

questions.question: Which of these nullifies wudhu?
options: A light nap while you still hear the class
questions.explanation: What exits from the private passages, including wind, breaks wudhu.

questions.question: Deep sleep breaks wudhu because…
options: The person no longer knows what is happening and control is lost
questions.explanation: Deep sleep is a nullifier. A light nap in which you still hear people is not.

questions.question: What is the ruling, in this lesson, on touching the private parts with the bare palm?
options: Nullifies wudhu in the teaching of this lesson
questions.explanation: It is listed among the nullifiers to write in the notebook.

questions.question: Wudhu is required before…
options: Swalah, if you are in minor impurity
questions.explanation: Purity is a condition of swalah. Touching the mushaf also requires wudhu in this teaching.

questions.question: Which time is recommended rather than a condition of the prayer?
options: Wudhu before Fajr if you need it
questions.explanation: Sleeping in wudhu is a recommended sunnah. Praying without required wudhu is not valid.

questions.question: Where is the advice to make wudhu when angry reported?
questions.explanation: It is a recommended help for calming anger, not a fifth pillar of swalah.

questions.question: Ghurra means…
options: Brightness from the traces of wudhu on the Day of Judgement
questions.explanation: The Prophet (S.A.W.) described his community as recognisable by these marks. The Hadith is in Sahih Muslim.

questions.question: Why is a correct wudhu linked with forgiveness?
options: The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that sins leave with the wudhu
It cancels the need to pray
questions.explanation: Sahih Muslim reports the forgiveness connected with performing wudhu properly.

questions.question: You are sure you had wudhu, then you only imagine that it might have broken. What do you do?
options: You must repeat every prayer of the week
Certainty of wudhu is not removed by a mere doubt
You stop praying for the day
You use soil while water is beside you
questions.explanation: A real nullifier breaks wudhu. A passing doubt does not.

questions.question: What does it mean to value purity as a condition for ibadah?
questions.answer: Performing wudhu properly before swalah and renewing it after a nullifier, because the prayer depends on that purity.
questions.explanation: Wudhu is not an optional extra when minor impurity is present.
